mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPI YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE drops > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% MoM signals a surge in demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases > 10% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a slowing economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO drops > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is above 2% YoY, it signals an accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% MoM, it signals a robust labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE drops > 0.3% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE drops > 0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which is a key driver of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 1% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy with weak economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with weak growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and GDPC1 YoY < 1%.
